name: Ninoy Aquino International Airport

runway.v: two runways; the main one, 06/24, is 3,737 m long and 60 m wide; 13/31 is 2,258 m long and 45 m wide
runway.quote: Runway 06/24. NAIA's primary runway is 3,737 meters long and 60 meters wide ... Runway 13/31. Its secondary runway is 2,258 meters long and 45 meters wide

ppr.v: non-scheduled flights (commercial and non-commercial) need MIAA approval of a flight advisory, filed at least 3 days ahead (2016 rule)
ppr.quote: Application must be filed in advance with a minimum notice period of three (3) days

handling.v: non-scheduled flights must use an MIAA-accredited ground handler or FBO (no names listed)
handling.quote: All Air Carriers or Operators of non-scheduled flights must secure the services of MIAA accredited Groundhandler/FBO

permits.v: a foreign operator may not start commercial air transport to the Philippines until a Validation of its Air Operator Certificate has been issued; the first application is due at least 90 days before operations start. The regulation does not mention non-scheduled or charter flights, so check how a single charter is treated (July 2025 edition)
permits.quote: No foreign air operator may commence commercial air transport operations in and to the Republic of the Philippines, ... until the Validation of Air Operator Certificate has been issued. ... at least ninety days before the date of commencement of intended operation.

missing: notable (GA peak-hour limits reported in news could not be confirmed from an official source)
notes: Philippine AIP needs a registered account (ais.caap.gov.ph), so no AD 2 data. NAIA has been run by a concessionaire since the O&M start date; the 2016 MIAA rules on flight advisories and FBOs may have been replaced by the concessionaire's rules - check before publishing. News reports of private-jet limits at NAIA are not used. 1 Nov 2026: re-read the MIAA NAIA PPP Information Memorandum (18 Sep 2023): no IATA code, hours, curfew, customs or GA rules in it; it says the runway system 'is currently limited to handling up to 40 commercial aircraft traffic movements (ATMs) per hour' (2023). The New NAIA Infra Corp. site (https://newnaia.com.ph/about-us/about-naia) gives no hours, IATA code or GA rules. Philippine AIP still needs a login. Private-jet limits at NAIA are only in news reports (Jan 2025), not used. | 2026-11-02 run: newnaia.com.ph about page re-read: metadata only, no hours, IATA or GA rules. Nothing new. 5 Nov 2026: added permits from PCAR Part 10 (July 2025 edition, newest found; a later edition may exist). Read with nothing on hours, curfew or slots: MIAA FAQ, MIAA Citizen's Charter 2025 (final 2,840 characters unread) and MIAA Revised Administrative Order No. 1 s.2024 (fees only; it defines General Aviation and lets the airport operator set FBO charges). CAB general FAQ has nothing on foreign non-scheduled flights. The 2016 MIAA rules on file are still unconfirmed under the concessionaire. CAAP Citizen's Charter 2026 failed at the site. Philippine News Agency reports on private planes were not used. | 7 Nov 2026: nothing added. MIAA Citizen's Charter 2026 (1st edition, first 100,000 characters read) lists no service for non-scheduled flights, general aviation or slots. MIAA 'NAIA Aerodrome' page loads only its heading; MIAA General Aviation page (https://www.miaa.gov.ph/index.php/terminals/general-aviation) failed at the site. MIAA MC 17 s.2023 is about waste management only. Private-jet limits at NAIA still only in news (not used).
